units.sourceLabel: UNIT 1 — Introduction, C Preliminaries and Operators
units.title: Introduction, C Preliminaries and Operators

overview.teaches: How a computer is organised, how binary represents information, how algorithms and flowcharts describe steps, and the first pieces of the C language: names, types, input/output, program structure, and operators.
overview.why: Later units assume you can already name parts of a machine, write a simple sequence of steps, and read a short C program.
prerequisites: Foundation: basic computer knowledge if the block diagram is unfamiliar.
outcomes: Name the main parts of a computer and what they do.
Explain why computers use binary.
Read a simple algorithm and flowchart.
Recognise C keywords, identifiers, constants, variables, and data types.
Read formatted input/output and the structure of a C program.
Evaluate arithmetic, assignment, relational, logical, increment, decrement, bitwise, and ternary operators at a beginner level.
overview.connectsTo: Unit 2 uses operators and type conversion inside decisions and loops.

units.sourceLabel: UNIT 2 — Conditional / Decision Statements and Control Structures
units.title: Conditional / Decision Statements and Control Structures

overview.teaches: How C chooses a path and how it repeats work: precedence, type conversion, if/switch, break/continue/goto, and loops.
overview.why: Almost every useful program must decide and repeat.
prerequisites: Unit 1 operators and a simple C program structure.
outcomes: Explain precedence and associativity with a small example.
Write if, if-else, nested if-else, else-if, and switch examples.
State what break, continue, and goto do, including why goto is usually avoided.
Trace while, do-while, and for loops.
overview.connectsTo: Unit 3 uses loops to walk through arrays and strings.

overview.teaches: One-dimensional and multi-dimensional arrays, string input/output, and string work with and without library functions.
overview.why: Lists of numbers and text are the usual way programs store many values.
prerequisites: Unit 2 loops and Unit 1 data types.
outcomes: Index a one-dimensional array.
Read a simple two-dimensional example.
Use string I/O carefully.
Use strlen, strcmp, strcat, strcpy; treat strrev as non-standard.
Perform simple string work without library functions.
overview.connectsTo: Unit 4 passes arrays into functions. Unit 5 searches and sorts arrays.

accuracyNotes: strrev() is not in the ISO C standard library. Label it as a compiler-specific / non-standard extension.

overview.teaches: Storage classes, how functions work, parameter passing, arrays as arguments, and recursion.
overview.why: Functions let you name a piece of work and reuse it. Storage classes control lifetime and visibility.
prerequisites: Unit 1–3: variables, arrays, and control flow.
outcomes: Describe auto, static, register, and extern with a small example each.
Write a function with a return value.
Explain call by value, and how pointers are used when teaching 'call by reference'.
Pass an array to a function.
Trace a small recursive function.
overview.connectsTo: Searching and sorting functions in Unit 5.
accuracyNotes: Standard C passes arguments by value. 'Call by reference' in the college wording is taught as passing an address (pointer) so the called function can change the caller's object.

overview.teaches: Linear and binary search, then bubble, insertion, selection, quick, and merge sort, plus laboratory / competitive practice as listed.
overview.why: Finding and ordering values is a core laboratory skill in this syllabus.
outcomes: Trace linear search and binary search.
Trace the five listed sorting methods at a beginner level.
